name: Orbit Capital
decision_note: Prague/Warsaw manager whose activity in the window is venture debt (Growth Debt II first close May 2025, second close EUR 107m July 2026, debt deals in Sloneek, IAG, Talkin' Things); under the revised E4 debt-focused funds incl. venture debt are excluded even with a legacy growth-equity book.

legal_entities.name: Conseq-Orbit SICAV, a.s. (LEI name: Orbit Capital SICAV, a.s.)
Conseq-Orbit SICAV, podfond Conseq Venture Debt

evidence.quote: Its focus will be on growth-stage software and other technology companies – a segment that across Europe faces a financing gap estimated at €1.4 trillion.
CEE investors Orbit Capital have announced the second closing of Growth Debt Fund II at €107 million, surpassing its initial target.
We issue initial tickets ranging from €8-15 million and currently support four companies: Booksy, MEWS, Preply, and Rohlik.
It will provide senior-debt financing to businesses to fuel their growth.
Fund II targets post-Series A technology companies with at least €3 million in revenue and a minimum 30 per cent YoY growth.
Founded in 2019, Orbit Capital manages both growth equity and venture debt funds, making it one of the few regional players offering non-dilutive financing to scaleups across CEE and DACH.

Fund II has already begun deploying capital, with 5 investments so far, including Czech startups Sloneek and IAG, as well as Polish startup Talkin' Things, further strengthening Orbit Capital’s portfolio of high-growth technology companies across the region.
Orbit Growth Debt II builds on a predecessor fund called Orbit Growth Debt I which a €40 million fund which started operations in 2019 and has invested in 15 Central European companies so far
With tickets ranging from €3 million to €15 million, the capital supports international expansion, acquisitions, working capital, and capital expenditures.

analyst_notes: Type vc chosen over pe: Orbit Growth Equity takes minority growth stakes (initial tickets EUR 8-15m, self-reported) in VC-backed tech scale-ups (Booksy, Mews, Preply, Rohlik), and Vestbee calls Orbit a venture capital fund family; it is not a buyout/majority investor. Excluded because all dated activity in the 24-month window is venture debt: Orbit Growth Debt II (EIF: 'senior-debt financing', first close 27 May 2025, EUR 70m per Vestbee 2025-06-17; second close EUR 107m announced 2026-07-02; 5 debt deals incl. Sloneek, IAG, Talkin' Things, dates not disclosed). Senior debt is not equity/quasi-equity (I2), hence E4 for the active strategy; the equity strategy shows no investment since 2024-10-25 (latest found: Rohlik Series D 2022), hence E7. If the pilot later counts venture debt as VC activity, this record would qualify. Ticket shown is the growth-equity ticket (self-reported, Startup Lithuania directory 2026-01-28); Growth Debt II tickets are EUR 3-15m (Tech.eu 2026-07-02), Growth Debt I EUR 3-7m per deal (same directory). Capital = Growth Debt II size (EUR 107m); growth-equity fund size not disclosed (CVCA 2020 profile: 'scaling to EUR 200 million'). Growth Debt I: EUR 40m, started 2019 (EIF), month unknown, date set to 2019-01-01. Legal entities: Conseq-Orbit SICAV a.s. (IČO 08223467) is registered in GLEIF as 'Orbit Capital SICAV, a.s.'; its sub-fund 'Conseq Venture Debt' (75161486) is presumably Orbit Growth Debt I; Orbit Growth SCSp (LU, created 2022-01-10) is presumably Growth Equity or Growth Debt II - mapping not confirmed. Own website orbitcapital.com is a JS-rendered page with almost no text, so no class B quote was usable. [revision 2026-10-25 after review: rule_codes E4+E7 -> E4 only. Policy decision in plan 10a: E4 covers debt-focused funds including venture debt, even with a legacy equity book, so the record stays excluded; E7 is dropped because Orbit is active (two Growth Debt II closes in the window; debt deals such as Sloneek (CZ, round co-led with VFF, 2026-06-16) and a tranche in Jutro Medical's Series A extension (Dec 2025), both per the reviewer and not itemised here).Capital note corrected: EUR 107m is the SECOND (interim) close of the venture-debt fund Growth Debt II (e3), not a final fund size, so basis interim_close and the fund event other -> interim_close. Ticket now the Growth Debt II ticket EUR 3-15m (e10) so that capital and ticket describe the same (debt) fund; the growth-equity ticket EUR 8-15m (self-reported, e4) belongs to the inactive equity strategy. Growth Debt I start date: only the year 2019 is known (e9), so the 2019-01-01 placeholder was removed (event_date null).]
